A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpatialJB and SpatialD, with matching core methods and experiments. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack evaluations across seven LLMs, a Claude ablation, and SpatialD defense experiments on JailBench in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline and guardrail evaluations, an AdvBench combination experiment, and additional attack demonstrations.

M1.justification: The six SpatialJB templates and SpatialD extraction/classification algorithms remain unchanged. v2 adds explicit combined attack procedures using FlipAttack or ArtPrompt to elicit content before SpatialJB formats it for delivery (Section 4.2; Figures 16–17), providing a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: The four hate/offensive-content datasets and JailBench are retained. v2 adds AdvBench evaluation of FlipAttack-generated harmful responses and demonstrations involving harmful instructional requests, extending attack coverage beyond the earlier toxic-text repetition and summarization tasks (Section 4.2; Figures 16–17).

E2.justification: PAP and SATA join Zulu, Base64, and Ubbi Dubbi in both Repeat and Summary comparisons. The evaluated defense set also expands from Llama Guard, OpenAI Moderation, and Perspective to include WildGuard and HarmAug, with reported scores in Tables 5–6.

E3.justification: v2 adds a conditional guardrail-bypass test on 521 FlipAttack-generated outputs and WildGuard/HarmAug evaluation configurations. The existing ASR formula and Perspective threshold remain unchanged. Appendix D.1.1 now specifies GPT-4o where v1 specified GPT-4, but v2's main text and tables retain GPT4, leaving actual model replacement or rerunning unresolved.

E4.justification: The original Claude module ablation and defense evaluation are retained. v2 adds a quantitative FlipAttack compatibility analysis, ArtPrompt combination demonstrations, and detailed acrostic, telestich, corner, and center case studies examining how harmful content survives spatial formatting (Section 4.2; Appendix F).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's newly reported human spot-check of 3% of results validates labels but provides no statistical uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 add baseline and guardrail scores, and Section 4.2 reports 415/521 outputs (79.65%) becoming guardrail-safe after SpatialJB. Retained Summary values also change: unguarded Grok4's six 75.0% entries become 72.6–75.7%, and DeepSeek-V3/Telestich under Llama Guard changes from 68.2% to 68.4%. Original Repeat, Claude ablation, and SpatialD values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The two original theoretical claims move into Appendix C with substantive additions: a formal visual-neighborhood definition, positional-distance assertions, an attention model incorporating an exponential locality factor, and a semantic aggregation expression. These extend the existing arguments without changing their principal conclusions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: SpatialJB exploits sequential-processing weaknesses through spatial formatting, achieves high attack success against LLMs and guardrails, and motivates SpatialD. Added experiments support the existing universality and compatibility claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets existing jailbreaks and SpatialJB as complementary elicitation and delivery mechanisms. Appendix F adds case-specific explanations of vertical masking and semantic dilution. The limitation that SpatialD's fixed extraction rules can miss misplaced harmful content was already stated in v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents the ASR extraction, word-check, semantic-check, and success-labeling procedure, including a 3% human audit. It expands SpatialD implementation explanations and concrete prompts/platform instructions. The abstract replaces the anonymous code pointer with a GitHub link and adds a demonstration-video link; these are documented access changes, not verified external availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for ArtPrompt, FlipAttack, PAP, SATA, WildGuard, HarmAug, and AdvBench, while revising background references. It explicitly positions SpatialJB as complementary to elicitation-stage attacks, while retaining the original spatial-guardrail motivation and overall related-work organization.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and background passages, expands the defense explanation, and condenses main-text proofs and experimental settings into summaries with fuller treatment in Appendices C–D. The original demo appendix moves from C to E, followed by new case-study and platform sections.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and appendix column layout, relocates and redraws figures, expands comparison-table columns, and separates compact main tables from full appendix tables. New ASR/framework diagrams, case figures, and platform screenshots substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Broader comparisons, the AdvBench compatibility experiment, and explicit evaluation and defense documentation make v2 more informative and assessable. The gain is limited by new inconsistencies: Appendix D.1.6 claims Llama Guard ASRs exceed 85% across models although Table 5 includes 57%, and GPT-4/GPT-4o specifications conflict between sections. The expanded theory also continues to rely on assumed exponential locality.
